workload.setup_in_timing: Every padding buffer zeroing and every input/output copy occurs within the timed call. Cipher/input reset setup occurs outside.
workload.order: Alternate all four policy orders between paired samples.
workload.runtime_key: Random startup key made opaque to compiler before cipher setup.

policy_descriptions.previous_decomposition: Frozen previous dispatch: 64-block sliced chunks, then 32/16/8/4-block matrix calls and scalar remainder. It shares the exact same production round kernels and keys, isolating the dispatch change.
policy_descriptions.original_multiple4: The original scratch proposal: round up to any multiple of four through width32 (including28/32), always preparing a padded temporary; otherwise padded64.
policy_descriptions.production: The actual Cipher.encryptBlocks/decryptBlocks API from the recorded source snapshot: 1 scalar; widths4/8/12/16/20/24, exact widths direct; larger tails padded64.
policy_descriptions.padded64: Always zero/copy valid inputs into the existing 64-block kernel and copy valid outputs back.
policy_descriptions.control_limit: The frozen-dispatch control receives a const Cipher pointer; production uses the actual public by-value entry. Tiny call-shape costs should not be interpreted as a regression against a compiled historic library.

checked_invariants: Public full-chunk loops reduce the remaining count to0..63 before entering the private tail helper.
Empty and single-block cases return before padded/vector handling.
The first fitting width4/8/12/16/20/24 handles every count2..24 and returns; exact-width inputs avoid temporary buffers.
Larger tails fit a64-block temporary. Every padded temporary is zeroed only at its selected width and only valid outputs are copied back.
Forward round keys, encryption/decryption direction,16-byte input alignment and the existing Cipher field layout are preserved.
The existing GFNI capability/backend condition retains the portable fallback; no new AVX-512VL condition is needed for this padding policy.

correctness.independent_check: Eight keys, every length0..63, four16-byte-aligned offsets, all four policies, arbitrary plaintext encryption and arbitrary ciphertext decryption; complete surrounding arrays compared with independent scalar oracle to verify guards. Narrow32 also checked at length32.
correctness.timed_outputs: Every timed policy output checksum agreed.

contention.coordination: The entire test VM was reserved for this replication. All compiler processes finished before timings; core0 was unused by this study.
contention.interpretation: Nine-sample medians are retained. Individual virtual-machine scheduling outliers are visible in the raw arrays; no claim of host-wide isolation is made.

narrow_control.workload: 32 useful blocks,9 samples of8388608 useful blocks. Shared crypto/kernel policies.
narrow_control.conclusion: NarrowYMM32 and padded existingZMM64 remain close; the simpler production policy avoids the extra architecture and feature gate.
narrow_control.build_note: Narrow controls were measured before the scalar-only update. These controls call only matrix/narrow/sliced kernels, which do not use that changed single-block scalar code.

scope: This independently confirms correctness and measured gains on a second Zen5 CPU. It is not a proof of physical optimality or universal performance on other microarchitectures.
validation_refresh: A scalar-only optimization landed during the first compile. This final table and all27tests were rebuilt and rerun with that current scalar source; tail helpers and round kernels were unchanged.
observations: Correctness review found no issue in the production padding and dispatch functions.
Material gains on padded and composite tails replicate; exact existing widths remain comparable. Very small differences remain within this VM study noise.

The production bulk API adds around2ns at length1 versus the direct frozen-dispatch wrapper, about4.4% encryption and2.2% decryption in the final run. This compares different wrapper call shapes; the single-block API itself is unaffected.
